headline: Quiet day today, just a few small tools
summary: No big launches. I picked 3 small things you can use right away even if you're not a developer.

items.title: Make Claude's designs look less like AI
items.pitch: Peter Yang rounded up 5 takeaways from Nate Parrott on how to get Claude to make pages that don't look like a generic AI template. You can use them right away for report pages or internal tools.
why: Start by giving Claude screenshots, pages you like, and your past work
For tricky layouts, have it look into how similar products do it first
No coding needed, you just change how you write your prompts
actions: Open the link and read all 5 tips, then next time you ask Claude to make a page, hand it some reference images first
deep_dive: This is a tips post, not a new tool. You can follow it with the Claude Code you're already using.
The source is secondhand, and only the first two of the 5 tips showed up in what I saw. You'll need to open the original post for the rest.
items.signals: Peter Yang's post has 138 likes · retells Nate Parrott's method

items.title: Gemini Notebook turns your materials into interactive web pages
items.pitch: Google's Josh Woodward showed a demo: drop your materials into Gemini Notebook and it makes an interactive website you can share.
why: You don't need to know how to code, and it's easy to make and share
Handy for turning training materials or pay policies into clickable pages
items.signals: Josh Woodward's post has 294 likes · official demo, no third-party testing yet
